title: Enrichment of aging yeast cells and budding polarity assay in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
protocol: Streak out the strains of interest on YPD plates from frozen stocks.
Seal plates with parafilm and incubate at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Inoculate several colonies into 5 mL of SC liquid media in a Falcon tube.
Loosen the cap on the Falcon tube.
Incubate the tube in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm at 30°C for 7–8 hours.
Measure the OD600 of the pre-culture.
Calculate the volume of pre-culture needed to achieve mid-log phase culture after overnight growth.
Inoculate calculated amount of pre-culture into fresh SC media to reach a final OD600 of 0.1–0.3.
Inoculate 25 mL of SC medium in a 100 mL sterile shake flask with 65 μL of pre-culture (OD600 = 0.3).
Grow the culture at 30°C with orbital shaking at 200 rpm for 16 hours.
Allow EZ-Link Sulfo-NHS-LC-LC-Biotin to reach a temperature between 20°C and 22°C.
Weigh 2 mg of Sulfo-NHS-LC-LC-Biotin.
Dissolve the biotin in 0.5 mL of PBS in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Rotate the tube at 20°C–22°C until the biotin is fully dissolved (5–10 minutes).
Seal the cap of the jar containing Sulfo-NHS-LC-LC-Biotin with parafilm.
Store the sealed Sulfo-NHS-LC-LC-Biotin container in a sealed container with desiccant at −20°C.
Transfer the Sulfo-NHS-LC-LC-Biotin container to room temperature within the dessicant-containing storage container.
Measure the OD600 of the overnight pre-culture.
Calculate the volume of culture corresponding to 4 OD600-mL.
Transfer 4 OD600 of cells to a fresh 50 mL Falcon tube or sterile SS34 centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 1,500 × g in a Sorvall ST 16 centrifuge (or equivalent) for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove supernatant carefully with a P1000 pipet.
Wash cells twice with 5 mL of 1× PBS containing 0.25% PEG3350.
Add 5 mL 1× PBS containing 0.25% PEG3350 to the Falcon tube and resuspend cells thoroughly.
Centrifuge the cells again at 1,500 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove supernatant carefully with a P1000 pipet.
Resuspend final cell pellet in 0.5 mL of 1× PBS.
Add resuspended cells to biotin solution from step 7.
Rotate the biotin-cell mixture in an orbital mixer for 30 min at 20°C–22°C.
Concentrate biotin-treated cells by centrifugation at 3,600 × g in a microcentrifuge for 1 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash cells once with 1 mL of 1× PBS containing 100 mM glycine.
Add 1 mL of 1× PBS containing 100 mM glycine to the cell pellet obtained from step 1.
Repeat steps 2–4.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL of 1× PBS containing 0.25% PEG3350 as described in step 7.
Resuspend biotin-labeled cells in 1 mL of growth media (SC).
Transfer resuspended cells to 500 mL of SC media in a 2-L sterile shake flask.
Grow cells at 30°C with orbital shaking at 200 rpm for 8–14 h.
Sterilize surroundings and gloves with 70% ethanol.
Use a Bunsen burner to maintain a sterile environment.
Transfer the 500 mL of liquid culture to 10 50-mL Falcon tubes or the appropriate number of sterilized reusable centrifuge tubes/bottles.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation at 1,500 × g in a Sorvall ST 16 centrifuge (or equivalent) for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Carefully decant supernatant.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 2 mL of SC.
Pool all cell suspensions in a 50-mL Falcon tube.
Wash Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 three times with growth media (SC).
Transfer 108 μL of Streptavidin Dynabeads to a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 mL of SC and vortex for more than 30 seconds.
Place the tube in a magnetic test tube rack for 1 minute to immobilize magnetic beads.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing steps with growth media (SC) two more times.
Resuspend washed Streptavidin Dynabeads in 0.5 mL of SC.
Transfer resuspended beads to the biotinylated cell suspension in the 50-mL Falcon tube.
Incubate the 50 mL Falcon tube in a rotary mixer for 15 min at 20°C–22°C.
Place ring magnets between the middle and top tiers of a poxygrid rack suitable for 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Transfer cells to a sterile mCAD glass vessel.
Place the vessel within ring magnets in the poxygrid tube rack and let stand for 5–10 min.
Gently tap and rotate the glass vessel to promote binding of the magnetic beads to the ring magnet.
Carefully remove all material that is not bound to the ring magnet using a 10-mL pipet.
Wash immobilized cells twice with SC.
Remove the glass vessel from the ring magnets and add 40 mL of SC to the glass vessel.
Place the glass vessel back into the ring magnets and let stand for 5–10 min.
Carefully remove media from the glass vessel using a 10-mL pipet.
Repeat steps of washing cells with SC as necessary.
Resuspend cells in 1–2 mL of SC media.
Prepare the magnetic cell attachment device (mCAD) as described.
Assemble the mCAD according to the provided instructions.
Ensure the mCAD is assembled and filled with media before introducing dynabead-bound cells.
Maintain the temperature at 20°C–22°C during operation of the mCAD.
Wear gloves.
Sterilize gloves and the bench with 70% ethanol.
Use a Bunsen burner to maintain a sterile environment.
Place ring magnets between the middle and top tiers of a poxygrid tube rack suitable for 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Remove all aluminum foil and autoclave tape from sterilized mCAD components.
Carefully open the sterile 2-L media bottle and add 2 L of sterile SC media.
Place the GL45 cap and its associated tubing on the media bottle and tighten it.
Tighten the Teflon cap on the mCAD vessel and place the sterilized mCAD vessel into the ring magnets in the poxygrid rack.
Insert the free end of the effluent tubing from the mCAD vessel into the waste flask and secure the tubing to the flask with tape.
Connect the air filter on the 16″ tubing to the free end of the 10″ tubing on the air pump and gauge assembly.
Connect the female luer on the free end of the peristaltic pump tubing to the 2–10″ connector tubing on the media bottle.
Insert the peristaltic pump tubing into the peristaltic pump for media flow from the media bottle through the peristaltic pump into the mCAD vessel.
Tighten the caps on the media bottle and mCAD vessel.
Turn on the peristaltic pump at a speed of 7 (flow rate x10 for a GE Healthcare peristaltic pump P-1) and air pump.
Check that media flows from the media bottle through the peristaltic pump to the mCAD vessel, and then out the effluent port into the waste flask as it fills with approximately 40 mL of media.
After filling, adjust the flow rate to ∼25 mL/h (speed 7, flow rate x1).
Ensure there are no leaks at connections or caps and that there is consistent positive pressure within the mCAD vessel.
Turn off the air and peristaltic pumps.
Clamp the effluent tubing with a tubing clamp.
Transfer the mCAD vessel from the ring magnets to a magnet-free location.
Remove the cap from the loading port on the mCAD vessel.
Use a 1-mL syringe to transfer streptavidin beads and their associated biotinylated cells from the 50-mL Falcon tube to the loading port.
Flush some air into the loading port using a sterile syringe to ensure all cells are in the medium within the mCAD vessel.
Place the cap on the loading port.
Place the mCAD vessel back into the ring magnets and let stand for 5–10 minutes.
Occasionally tap and rotate the glass vessel or turn on the air pump at its lowest setting to promote circulation and binding of magnetic beads and their associated cells to the ring magnets.
Remove the clamp from the effluent tubing.
Ensure that the caps on the media bottle and mCAD vessel are tightly closed.
Turn on the air and peristaltic pumps.
Set the air pump pressure to 0.7–0.8 PSI.
Set the flow rate on the peristaltic pump to approximately 25 mL/h (For a GE Healthcare-peristaltic pump P-1: speed 7, flow rate x1).
Let the system run for 24–56 hours.
Check the system daily for leaks and ensure there is sufficient media in the media bottle.
Harvest desired populations of yeast cells.
Use a fresh 50-mL Falcon tube to collect young cells from the effluent tubing when harvesting daughter cells.
Turn off both pumps and clamp the effluent port with a tubing clamp.
Remove the mCAD vessel from the ring magnet, swirl to resuspend cells in the media, and tilt the vessel to submerge the needle tip of the loading port into the media.
Withdraw cells from the mCAD vessel using a 5- or 10-mL Luer-lock syringe based on the number of time points needed for the experiment.
Transfer harvested cells to a fresh sterile glass vessel.
Insert the vessel into the ring magnets and allow it to stand for 5–10 min.
Remove all material that is not bound to the ring magnet using a 10-mL transfer pipet.
Wash immobilized cells twice with 40 mL of SC.
Remove the glass vessel from the ring magnets, wash the walls of the glass vessel, and resuspend cells in 1–2 ml of SC media.
Carefully remove the Teflon cap, tubing, and bubble cage from the mCAD glass vessel without disturbing cells that are immobilized within the vessel.
Remove media from the mCAD glass vessel using a 10 mL pipet.
Remove the ring magnets and resuspend cells in the glass vessel with 30 mL of SC media.
Place the glass vessel in the ring magnets and let stand for 5–10 min to immobilize biotinylated mother cells.
Repeat steps 48-50 at least 4 times.
Resuspend washed cells in 1 mL of SC media.
Transfer 0.5–1 OD600-mL of isolated yeast cells in 1 mL of SC medium to a fresh 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Add AlexaFluor 488-WGA (2 μL of 1.09 mM stock) and mix.
Stain cells for 15 min at 20°C–22°C.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation at 3,600 × g in a microcentrifuge for 1 min at 20°C–22°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash cell pellet 3 times with SC media.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of SC.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation at 3,600 × g in a microcentrifuge for 1 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Repeat steps a-c 2 times.
Resuspend the washed cell pellet in 1 mL of SC.
Transfer cells to a 50 mL Falcon tube and dilute cells to a final volume of 5 mL.
Grow cells at 30°C with orbital shaking at 200 rpm for 2 h.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation at 1,500 × g in a Sorvall ST 16 centrifuge (or equivalent) for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL SC.
Stain cells with AlexaFluor 594-WGA for 15 min.
Wash the stained cells.
Resuspend the washed cells as described in step 57.
Centrifuge stained cells at 3,600 × g for 1 minute at 20°C–22°C.
Remove supernatant, leaving 10-20 μL in the tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the remaining medium.
Transfer 1.8 μL of resuspended cells to a microscope slide.
Cover the sample with a #1.5 coverslip for imaging.
Image each slide for 10 min or less.
Suspend cells in a small volume of medium (1.8 μL) for imaging.
Locate a field of cells and acquire a z-series using the following settings: WGA-AlexaFluor 488, excitation/emission 470/507 nm, 50% power, typical exposure time 300 ms.
Acquire WGA-AlexaFluor 594 z-stacks with excitation/emission 561/610 nm, 50% power, typical exposure time 300 ms.
Use 1 × 1 binning for final pixel dimensions less than 0.1 μm.
Capture 21-27 z sections with 0.3 μm spacing.
Acquire AlexaFluor 594 and AlexaFluor 488 z-stacks sequentially for speed and stability.
Adjust power settings and exposure times based on signal intensity.
Acquire 2–3 images per slide.
Image 5–6 slides per sample to capture approximately 100 cells.
Open microscopic images in FIJI using the Bio-Formats importer: Plugins → Bio-Formats →Bio-Formats Importer.
Make a composite image: Image → Color → Make Composite.
Adjust visible channels by Channel tool… (Figure 5[href=https://www.wicell.org#fig5]A).
Create a maximum projection image: Image → Stacks → Z Project… Select Max intensity. (Figure 5[href=https://www.wicell.org#fig5]B).
Define the unit: Analyze → Set Scale... In our system, 1 pixel = 0.0645 μm.
Measure the diameter of the mother cell using the Straight line tool.
Analyze the measurement results: Analyze → Measure (Figure 5[href=https://www.wicell.org#fig5]A).
Count bud scars on Z-projected and Z-stack images.
Score at least 50 cells for each age group per genotype.
